candidates.description: A whimsical children's-book pirate tale in which 'Tom Tomb' and 'Dingy David' plunder domestic-scale seas (the 'Dining-room Carpetwaters,' 'Kitchen Archipelago') with nonsense vocabulary and cartoonish exaggeration. The playful frame treats the domestic household as a piratical geography.

novelty.rationale: The imaginative renaming of household rooms as seas is comic metaphor and nonsense whimsy, not a totalizing, world-altering difference from the empirical norm. Nothing in the storyworld is systematically changed; the setting remains an ordinary cottage and coast treated humorously.

cognitive_validation.rationale: There is no systematic, immanent account of any imaginary science or alternative social organization. The invented words (cinderadustmat, ockapillies, acquadatoric) are pure nonsense with no coherent internal logic, functioning as comedic decoration rather than a cognitively validated novum.

narrative_hegemony.rationale: The narrative logic is driven by conventional comic melodrama—capture, romance, reunion of a noble family—not by any estranging novum. No world-altering difference governs the plot.

estrangement.rationale: Any contrast the reader perceives is comic/whimsical (nonsense words, domestic geography played as high-seas adventure), not cognitive estrangement in Suvin's sense. This is a humorous children's picture book, not science fiction.
